item.title: Most consecutive wins to start a Premier League season
item.description: Most consecutive wins to start a Premier League season Manchester City head to Aston Villa this lunchtime aiming to continue a perfect start to the Premier League season. Enzo Maresca's men have won all seven games so far this season to take an early lead in the title race. The Italian's flawless record means Manchester City have already recorded the third-best start to a Premier League campaign, in terms of consecutive wins from the opening weekend. Chelsea hold the all-time record after winning their opening nine games in 2005/06. Fresh from winning the Premier League title under Jose Mourinho, Chelsea made a dream start to their defence, winning their opening nine games before a 1-1 draw at Everton. The Blues won 20 of their first 22 games overall on route to a second straight championship. City can match Liverpool 's eight-win record from 2019/20 today. Jurgen Klopp's side secured eight consecutive wins to start the season, before drawing at Manchester United. That season saw Liverpool record the best-ever start to a campaign in Europe's top five leagues, after taking 79 points from a possible 81 (26 wins, one draw) before being beaten by Watford. Liverpool ended the campaign on 99 points to secure a first league title in 30 years. Manchester City now have the opportunity to join that illustrious company. But where do City’s current run and the Premier League’s other historic starts rank among the best? From Chelsea’s dominant title defences to Liverpool’s march towards the 2019/20 championship, these are the teams to have recorded the most consecutive wins from the opening weekend of a Premier League season. *Manchester City's winning run is ongoing

item.title: Where to watch Ferris State vs. Michigan Tech: Channel, live stream, time, schedule for D2 Top 25 matchup
item.description: Where to watch Ferris State vs. Michigan Tech: Channel, live stream, time, schedule for D2 Top 25 matchup originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michigan Tech has already pulled off the upset of the season in the GLIAC, and the Huskies will try to top it Saturday against No. 1 Ferris State. The two-time defending national champions have won 37 games in a row but are coming off their closest game in about a year, a 41-34 triumph in their annual rivalry game against Grand Valley State. That was the second consecutive loss for the Lakers, who fell the previous week at Michigan Tech in overtime. GVSU was ranked No. 6 in Division II at the time, and that victory combined with last weekend's rout of Northern Michigan have helped the Huskies move up to No. 12 in the AFCA poll. Twin brothers Elliott and Abram Larner power the Michigan Tech offense along with Elliott's fellow quarterback Alex Bueno. Elliott Larner is the Huskies' running QB, leading the team with 567 yards and 14 TDs on the ground at 6.5 yards per carry (plus 496 more yards through the air). Bueno is the primary passer, racking up 675 yards through the air and seven TDs. Abram Larner is the top target for both QBs with 37 receptions for 588 yards and eight touchdowns. Ferris knows plenty about dual-threat quarterbacks, as Wyatt Bower is in the midst of another spectacular season. The redshirt freshman has 1,980 yards and 21 TDs through the air, plus 800 yards and 15 more touchdowns on the ground. Add in Chase Carter's 1,181 rushing and 972 passing yards with 33 total TDs and the Bulldogs have two top-end QBs. It's a lot to stop, and no one has managed to do it yet, but Michigan Tech will give it a shot Saturday. Here's all you need to know to watch. Where to watch Ferris State vs. Michigan Tech TV channel: None Live stream: FloCollege Ferris State vs. Michigan Tech won't air on traditional television but can be streamed live on FloCollege. New subscribers can get a 15 percent discount on a FloCollege annual subscription through The Sporting News' exclusive offer. Purchasing a FloCollege subscription gives sports fans access to live streams, event replays and FloSports Originals. Ferris State vs. Michigan Tech start time Date: Saturday, Oct. 24 Time: 1 p.m. ET Ferris State vs. Michigan Tech will kick off Saturday at 1 p.m. ET. The game will be played at Top Taggart Field in Big Rapids, Michigan. Ferris State football schedule 2026 Here are the Bulldogs' upcoming games: Date Game Time (ET) Oct. 31 vs. Davenport 1 p.m. Nov. 7 at Wayne State 1 p.m. Nov. 14 vs. Roosevelt 1 p.m. Michigan Tech football schedule 2026 Here are the Huskies' upcoming games: Date Game Time (ET) Oct. 31 at Saginaw Valley State 1 p.m. Nov. 7 vs. Davenport 12 p.m. Nov. 14 vs. Wayne State 12 p.m. Related Links Latest college football news Updated Top 25 rankings College football schedule, scores How to bet on college football

item.description: Today’s Papers – Juventus injury crisis deepens as Torino fly La Gazzetta dello Sport Max and Gasp The laws of goals Allegri’s obsession with the result against Gasperini’s intensity Inter, another title first, but Lazio can overtake them at the top. Toro fly Three more goals, third win in a row: Juve overtaken. Galliani on the pitch The idea in Serie A emerges: Malagò ready for the challenge on the vote Corriere dello Sport Exclusive Pioli ‘I’m thirsty for revenge’ ‘I was the one who made mistakes in Florence; I still have a lot to give.’ He has just turned 61: ‘I feel young; I want to redeem myself, possibly in Italy. The Scudetto with Milan was the peak.’ ‘With people like Cristiano, Ibra, Klose and Giroud, it’s easier to win. Football has changed a lot. I’ve understood one thing about Fabregas and why he’ll have a great career.’ Rino tries to run away If he wins, he’ll go to the top alone for one night: ‘I want the same energy as in Turin.’ Max-Gasp: A Clasico Allegri with KDB as a regista, there’s Anguissa, out Lobotka. Gian Piero with Mora and Soulé behind Malen. Conte: ‘No negotiations in advanced stage.’ Tuttosport Juve, go get yourself blessed The injury crisis deepens: Nico and Celik out too, Sarr a doubt for Lecce The Argentine (problem with the soleus muscle) and the Turkish (femoral bicep) out until the break. Adductor problem for the Senegalese. The Bianconeri players have already missed 59 games. Woltemade is training in the penalty area; tomorrow he’ll partner Kolo. Terrific Toro: you dream like this! Fitz-Jim, Belghali, Vlasic: Three super goals crush Monza: 6th spot for a night, +2 on Juve. Three consecutive Serie A wins after seven years. Fan enthusiasm returns; celebration under the Maratona. Abate got everything right: ‘What a reaction after Varela’s 1-1, what a soul!’ Vlasic: ‘I missed scoring a goal; it was nice to see our fans happy again.’ Belghali: ‘I hope to score more goals like this.’ Juric: ‘Nothing to say, they were better than us.’ Gattuso and Gilardino: World Cup turnaround Maignan apologises, shame on social media Racist comments towards the Milan keeper after the Bournemouth madness. item.title: Xabi Alonso admits Real Madrid exit came too soon as he reflects on his dismissal: ‘I don’t look back in anger’
item.description: Xabi Alonso admits Real Madrid exit came too soon as he reflects on his dismissal: ‘I don’t look back in anger’ Former Real Madrid manager Xabi Alonso has admitted that his time at the Santiago Bernabeu ended earlier than he expected. After Alonso established himself as a top manager at Bayer Leverkusen, Los Blancos took a punt on the Spaniard at the beginning of last season. However, Xabi’s time at the club started brightly during the Club World Cup before eventually fading away, leading to his sacking in January after the Spanish Super Cup final. Alonso believes he deserved more time at Real Madrid In a recent interview, Alonso reflected on his departure and the unusual demands of managing Madrid. “I felt as though it finished a little bit earlier, before knowing if the season was going to end well,” Alonso explained (h/t Madrid Zone ). “It was the middle of the season. We were still in La Liga, the Champions League, but it was an experience.” Alonso’s comments clearly indicate that the timing of his departure remains a disappointment, especially with Los Blancos still in the running for major trophies. Xabi Alonso is doing well at Chelsea. (Photo by Ayush Kumar/Getty Images) Despite the disappointment, the Chelsea manager insists that he holds no resentment towards the club. “Real Madrid is special in everything. It is a little bit different to other clubs in everything,” he said. “I learned from that, and I don’t look back in anger. I look back, thinking I tried and gave my best.” Alonso’s comments highlight the pressure of managing Madrid Alonso’s reflections show just how demanding the Madrid job can be for a new manager and that he looks back positively on the experience. At the Bernabeu, competing for trophies is rarely enough on its own. Results, performances and the ability to manage a dressing room full of established stars are all paramount. Jose Mourinho is the exact polar opposite to Xabi Alonso. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His departure also raises a reasonable question about patience. Xabi came to Madrid with a clear plan and a desire to change the style of football at the club. However, less than halfway through the campaign, Madrid lost patience and sacked him , only to turn to Alvaro Arbeloa. Jose Mourinho’s subsequent appointment suggests the club felt they had made a mistake with Alonso and wanted to head in a completely different direction. His tenure ended without the opportunity to complete the season, but Alonso has started well at Chelsea, and Madrid fans will wish him nothing but the best in his career.

item.title: ‘The Disrespect for Our Country Is Wild,’ ‘Move On’ — WNBA Fans Divided Over Gabby Williams’ Response to National Anthem Controversy
item.description: Oct 2, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams (1) before game three of the first round for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs at Chase Center. © Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream reportedly stayed off the court during the national anthem before each of the first three WNBA Finals games, drawing questions about the teams’ pregame routine. Golden State forward Gabby Williams addressed the issue Friday after a reporter asked whether the team’s absence was a protest. Her response prompted mixed reactions from WNBA fans. Gabby Williams’ Response to National Anthem Question Divides WNBA Fans OutKick’s Dan Zaksheske reported on X that he asked Williams whether the Valkyries’ absence during the national anthem was a protest. The two-time All-Star answered, “No.” When Zaksheske followed up by asking why the team was not on the court, Williams explained, “That’s been the routine for like, seven years now.” According to Zaksheske, a Golden State public relations representative responded to further questioning with, “Next question.” One user criticized the team’s absence, writing, “All athletes should be mandated to be on the court during the playing of the national anthem. This disrespect for our country is wild. Makes it hard to support the WNBA of this is the norm.” Others questioned why the issue was being raised during the Finals. “Gabby is funny as hell she’s like ? This is such a (expletive) question,” one fan wrote . Another added , “Ik this was Gabby in her head when the question was asked. But genuinely why ask about the national anthem? Like she does not care, now move on.” The exchange also drew reactions to Williams’ demeanor during the interview. “These interviews are getting funnier and funnier dawg Gabby was done with him,” one user remarked . Williams’ reference to a seven-year routine prompted questions about the Valkyries’ relatively short history. Golden State is only in its second season, but Williams did not specify whether she meant the Valkyries or a broader trend in the WNBA. “How can it have been the routine for seven years with an organization that is just wrapping up its second season? i’m telling you, most players just go with the flow but have no real answer as the why they aren’t participating when the anthem is played,” one fan questioned . Another fan asked , “7 years? The Valks have only existed 2 years.” The WNBA’s anthem procedures have changed over time. The WNBA’s 2026 rulebook still states that players, coaches, and trainers are to stand and line up along the sidelines or foul line during the national anthem. However, the Associated Press reported that the league suspended its anthem protocols late in 2017, and it remains unclear how the provision currently applies or is enforced It remains unclear whether any current policy requires players to be on the court. SEE ALSO: ‘Stephanie White Is Next,’ ‘One of the Worst GMs’ – WNBA Fans React to Amber

SEE ALSO: ‘Stephanie White Is Next,’ ‘One of the Worst GMs’ – WNBA Fans React to Amber Cox’s Firing As Fever Undergo Massive Front Office Overhaul Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase also described the practice as part of the team’s pregame routine. “We’re two years in. Meanwhile, Atlanta leads the best-of-seven Finals 2-1, with Game 4 scheduled for Saturday at State Farm Arena. Williams has averaged a team-best 21.2 points per game this postseason as Golden State looks to level the series in the franchise’s first Finals appearance. item.title: Fastest pitch in World Series history as Brewers win opener
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers' starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski led Major League Baseball with 252 strikeouts in the regular season [Getty Images] Milwaukee Brewers starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski threw the fastest recorded pitch in World Series history as his side began the best-of-seven season finale with a win. The right-hander played a starring role in the 3-2 win at home to the Tampa Bay Rays, in the first match of the 122nd World Series. It is only the second time in more than a century that neither side contesting the World Series has won the title before. A sell-out crowd watched the Brewers in only their second appearance in the finale of the Major League Baseball season, and their first since losing to the St Louis Cardinals in 1982. Milwaukee's American Family Field has 41,900 seats but with standing-room-only tickets available for the 'Fall Classic', 43,250 fans packed in to see the game. "It was amazing - just to have the city behind me, it means the world, we couldn't ask for anything better," said Misiorowski. The Brewers host the second match of the best-of-seven series on Saturday before the teams move to Florida for three games, then return to Milwaukee for the final two matches, if needed. Misiorowski, 24, became the youngest starter since 1997 to win a World Series opener, after restricting the Rays to just one run in five innings. His fastest pitch at 103.5 mph beat the previous mark of 103.2 mph set by Aroldis Chapman of the Chicago Cubs in 2016 - though speeds have only been recorded since 2008. Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich also played a key role, scoring one run and driving in another as they took a 3-1 lead. The Rays added one run in the final inning and had a runner on third base as they pushed to level the score, but Milwaukee closed out victory. "It feels great. The guys settled in right away and did a great job," Yelich said. "We've still got a ways to go but nice to get that first one." The Brewers made the World Series by beating the Los Angeles Dodgers 4-0 to claim the National League title, while the Rays clinched the American League pennant with a 4-2 win over the Cleveland Guardians to reach the post-season finale for only the third time. The Rays lost to the Philadelphia Phillies in the 2008 World Series and the Dodgers in 2020, but manager Kevin Cash took solace from the fact that they tested the Brewers on Friday. "We came up a little bit short, but there's some benefit maybe from a loss," said Cash.

item.title: 'They can't fool me!' - Rodri warns Barcelona team-mates over Real Madrid trap ahead of El Clasico clash
item.description: Rodri - Getty Images Rodri has warned his Barcelona teammates not to be deceived by Real Madrid’s inconsistent start to the season ahead of Sunday’s massive El Clasico. The veteran midfielder, who joined the Catalan giants this summer, believes his club's arch-rivals often lure opponents into a false sense of security before striking. Rodri embraces Clasico challenge The 30-year-old midfielder is preparing for his maiden Clasico after swapping Manchester City for Catalonia this summer. While Barcelona boast a flawless LaLiga record, Real Madrid have already suffered two domestic defeats. Despite the contrasting league form, the World Cup-winning Spain captain is acutely aware of the threat posed by their fierce rivals. The fixture holds extra significance for the veteran, who was heavily linked with a move to the Spanish capital before ultimately choosing Barcelona . "I've played in plenty of knockout ties against them and I realise that one of their great strengths is making their opponents think they aren't that good," he said. "They don't fool us - or at least they don't fool me. Real Madrid are always a formidable opponent, whatever form they're in." The former City star also highlighted his personal excitement ahead of Sunday's showdown. "I've watched it loads of times on the television, as a fan when I was little, and as I've grown up, I've followed both teams," he added. "It's always a special match to play in, whether you're on one side or the other, so I'm really happy." Addressing his wider impact since arriving in Spain, Rodri pinpointed his veteran presence as a key asset. "I think the main thing I bring to this team is my experience, that leadership role, organising my team-mates and instilling a positive mindset in them," he said. Keeping feet firmly on the ground Barcelona are chasing a third consecutive La Liga crown, but the dressing room is refusing to get carried away by their early advantage. Teenage defender Pau Cubarsi acknowledged the points gap but insisted focus must remain absolute, telling ESPN : "It is a very big gap, but La Liga is a long season... anything can change at any moment in La Liga, and we have to maintain our momentum." item.title: ‘Lamar Jackson Fries Ian Rapoport for Lying,’ ‘Dark Day for Reporters’ — NFL World Reacts As Ravens Superstar Refutes Insider’s Injury Update
item.description: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Lamar Jackson has found himself at the center of an injury-report controversy, and the Baltimore Ravens quarterback isn’t staying quiet about it. Jackson is still working his way back from an ankle issue, but he recently pushed back against Ian Rapoport’s report about its severity, saying his own trainers gave him a different diagnosis. Lamar Jackson Challenges Ian Rapoport’s Injury Report Jackson injured his left ankle during Baltimore’s Oct. 4 win over the Tennessee Titans and missed the next two games. Rapoport had reported that the injury was neither a high-ankle nor a low-ankle sprain. Jackson, however, said the Ravens’ medical staff gave him a different diagnosis. When a reporter asked about the discrepancy, Jackson questioned Rapoport’s source while making it clear that he was going with what his own medical staff told him. “Rapoport said that? He part of the training staff?” Jackson asked. “So we can’t go off Ian Rapoport and his reporting. Somebody probably told him that too, though, so I can’t blame him. But nah, man, my staff told me it was a high-ankle sprain, so we’re going with what [head certified athletic trainer] Adrian [Dixon] told me.” Jackson’s comments drew reactions from analysts and Ravens fans alike, with some pointing out how the original report may have shaped perceptions of his recovery. Physical therapist Jeff Mueller said the situation showed how easily information can get lost or changed as it passes from sources to reporters and then to fans. He wrote on X , “Great reminder that telephone between (source) and NFL insider often relays wrong information, and then, we intake wrong information as audience. If it was initially reported as a high ankle sprain, no one would be surprised that Lamar Jackson has missed this much time.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Meanwhile, Ravens podcast host Samuel Njoku was fed up with the uncertainty surrounding the quarterback’s injuries, posting , “Always ‘misinformation and speculation’ when it comes to Lamar injuries.” Rob Pizzola saw Jackson’s response as a win for the medical staff and a tough moment for NFL reporters. He wrote , “Patient overrides the insider report with his own trainer’s diagnosis. Huge win for the medical community. Dark day for reporters.” Tom Strachan took a more playful approach to the exchange, writing , “Lamar from the top rope for Rapsheet.” A fan account, LamarOnReal, was more direct, accusing Rapoport of lying about the injury . Strength and conditioning coach Garrett Ferguson also questioned the earlier coverage, writing , “I hate to say it, but we owe Mike Florio an apology because he said Lamar Jackson’s ankle injury was a multiple-week concern. item.title: Friday’s LSU vs. Auburn injury report: Trey’Dez Green still not listed
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 17: Trey'Dez Green #7 of the LSU Tigers in action against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Tiger Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images) The final injury report is out for LSU vs Auburn in Jordan-Hare Stadium this Saturday. Kickoff is for 11 am central. The biggest news is the removal of Trey’Dez Green. This is something to monitor throughout the week to see if he pops back up based on his potential return to practice, but it appears as if the Tigers could be getting their star tight end back earlier than they anticipated. Princewill Umanmielen and Jackson Harris both not being listed on the injury report is important to note, as well. Both left the game early against Mississippi St last week, but appear to be back healthy and ready to go. LSU Out LB #7 Whit Weeks S #10 Dashawn Spears WR #15 Phillip Wright III LB #26 Charles Ross II DT #88 Richard Anderson Although it initially appeared as if Anderson was missing for family matters, which still is a part of it, it was discovered that he actually is injured. It’s unclear what exactly is injured, but it looks as if he’ll be out for a decent amount of time. Auburn Out OL #71 Tai Buster TE #85 Hunter Herring DL #99 Saint Farrior

item.title: Alex Marquez says overtaking Marc Marquez was “too risky” in Australian GP sprint
item.description: Motorsport photo Alex Marquez has admitted that he did not attempt a move on his elder brother Marc Marquez in the Australian Grand Prix sprint, saying he found it “too risky” to pull off a pass on a title contender. A tight battle between championship rivals Marc Marquez and Jorge Martin brought Gresini rider Alex Marquez into play in Saturday’s half-distance race at Phillip Island, with the 30-year-old closing in significantly on them by lap 8. Martin’s subsequent crash out of second put the four-time grand prix winner right behind his brother, but the pair maintained their positions in the closing stages, finishing just three tenths adrift as the chequered flag flew on lap 13. The race significantly boosted Marc Marquez’s hopes of winning his 10th world title, as he moved 10 points clear of Aprilia rival Martin in the standings. After the sprint, Alex Marquez admitted he deliberately stayed behind his brother’s factory Ducati, insisting he had no intention of attempting a pass that could affect the latter’s title chances. “From the beginning, I was feeling really good, really on pace, with a really good feeling on the bike, and I was able to be there,” said the Gresini rider. “I lost a little bit too much time with the fight with Acosta, and then the gap was big to Jorge and Marc. “I just tried to keep the pace there, and I was able to close the gap again, also [helped by] the overtakes that they did. “In the end, I was there with Marc, but it was too risky to try to overtake him, him playing for a championship. So that's it, I arrived second, and I was able to keep the pace until the end.” Watch: Marc Márquez on Retirement, Acosta and the Next King of MotoGP Alex Marquez lined up second on the grid and dropped to fourth at the start, before repassing Johann Zarco and Martin on lap 2 to retake the position. Martin fought back immediately afterwards and demoted him back to third, but the younger Marquez remained in the hunt through the middle stages of the race. After Martin’s retirement, he remained within striking distance of race leader Marc Marquez, but settled for a safe second position ahead of VR46’s Fabio di Giannantonio . Asked whether he felt he was quicker than the new championship leader, Alex Marquez said: “Maybe one tenth, two tenths - one and a half. “But also it's true that when I did that push lap to try to close the gap again, I used a little bit too much energy and too much rear tyre at that moment. I arrived in the end a little bit too on the limit. “It's true that in the beginning when I overtook Jorge, my idea was to also overtake Marc, and try to push my rhythm, because in that feeling I was feeling faster than them, and just try to put my rhythm. “But when I overtook Jorge, he overtook me again on turn 4. So I was not able to really defend or to make a small gap to him.” Aprilia had emerged as the manufacturer to beat at the start of the Phillip Island weekend, with the Noale-based factory finishing 1-2-4-5 in Practice.

However, the tables were turned on Saturday, with Ducati locking out the podium positions in the sprint race. A wet qualifying worked in the favour of the Borgo Panigale manufacturer, allowing Marquez to claim pole position while consigning Marco Bezzecchi and Ai Ogura to ninth and 12th on the grid, respectively. Injury also forced Raul Fernandez to retire from the sprint, leaving Bezzecchi as the marque’s best-finisher in fourth. But Alex Marquez believes Aprilia still has a performance advantage at Phillip Island, having closely followed the battle between Martin and his elder brother. “I think they still have it [an advantage],” he said. “I saw it from behind that maybe Jorge had something in some corners, but he was not able to make a gap to Marc. “So, we just try to defend what we have, and just try to be there. Three Ducatis on the sprint podium, so not bad.” Read Also: Marc Marquez: Jorge Martin was faster but overriding in Australian GP sprint Jorge Martin declared unfit for Australian GP after suffering fracture in sprint To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Juve full-back, Ramos decision, Allegri rejects Lobotka? Morning news ☀️
item.description: Juve full-back, Ramos decision, Allegri rejects Lobotka? Morning news ☀️ After Torino beat Monza 3-2 in Friday's opener, Serie A's eighth round gets into full swing with four matches on Saturday. Watch every Serie BKT match live with LaB Channel on OneFootball: subscribe for just €9.99 a month! The weekend's matches are just one of the topics in this morning's press review. Here are the biggest stories involving the top clubs. Juventus eye Araujo for the left flank One of Juventus' main priorities for the January transfer window is to strengthen their full-back options with quality players. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Sporting's Maxi Araujo is on their radar alongside Tagliafico and Ait-Nouri. It would have to be a permanent deal for a sizeable fee, only possible if Cabal is sold. Milan's big names return in Udine: four key players to start As reported by Corriere dello Sport, Milan will put any lineup experiments aside against Udinese. Mario Gila will feature in defence, with Modric in midfield and Rabiot in an attacking midfield role. Up front, Goncalo Ramos is back fit and will start. Inter: Provedel's time has come According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Cristian Chivu has decided to start rotating his goalkeepers now that Josep Martinez has regained confidence through his performances. Ivan Provedel will make his Serie A debut for Inter against Fiorentina. The goalkeeper will also play against Venezia, while Pepo will return to the starting lineup for the derby against Milan. Napoli: Allegri benches Lobotka again A Napoli side with Stanislav Lobotka left out for tactical reasons once seemed unthinkable, yet it will now happen for the second game in a row. As Corriere dello Sport reports, Kevin De Bruyne will once again take the Slovak's place in the deep-lying playmaker role. It is a bold decision, driven by Allegri's desire to find the ideal position for the Belgian star. Roma's big-game defence returns After rotating against Genoa and Slovan Bratislava, Roma will restore their first-choice defence against Napoli, Gazzetta dello Sport reports. Mancini, Ndicka and Hermoso will be on the pitch together for the first time since the Real Madrid match, when a 3-1 lead turned into a 4-3 defeat, partly as a result of defensive substitutions. Lazio: Gattuso sticks with his men As Gazzetta dello Sport points out, Gennaro Gattuso has complete faith in the new starters who have taken Lazio to the top of the table. Players such as Sutalo, Belahyane and Isaksen are currently untouchable, despite the returns of Doekhi, Cataldi and Cancellieri giving him options to rotate. Fiorentina: Vanoli keeps faith with Pellegrino Despite his subdued performance against Como, Mateo Pellegrino will also start for Fiorentina against Inter. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, coach Paolo Vanoli intends to favour the Argentine striker over Beto. Now, though, he is looking for a response, perhaps with a first Serie A goal since the match against Venezia. This article was

As Corriere dello Sport reports, Kevin De Bruyne will once again take the Slovak's place in the deep-lying playmaker role. It is a bold decision, driven by Allegri's desire to find the ideal position for the Belgian star. Roma's big-game defence returns After rotating against Genoa and Slovan Bratislava, Roma will restore their first-choice defence against Napoli, Gazzetta dello Sport reports. Mancini, Ndicka and Hermoso will be on the pitch together for the first time since the Real Madrid match, when a 3-1 lead turned into a 4-3 defeat, partly as a result of defensive substitutions. Lazio: Gattuso sticks with his men As Gazzetta dello Sport points out, Gennaro Gattuso has complete faith in the new starters who have taken Lazio to the top of the table. Players such as Sutalo, Belahyane and Isaksen are currently untouchable, despite the returns of Doekhi, Cataldi and Cancellieri giving him options to rotate. Fiorentina: Vanoli keeps faith with Pellegrino Despite his subdued performance against Como, Mateo Pellegrino will also start for Fiorentina against Inter. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, coach Paolo Vanoli intends to favour the Argentine striker over Beto. Now, though, he is looking for a response, perhaps with a first Serie A goal since the match against Venezia. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Portage Week 10 football roundup, Streetsboro seals share of MAC title
item.description: In addition to our live coverage of Ravenna-Roosevelt , here's a look at what happened in other Portage County high school football games in Week 10: Watch Ohio High School Sports Live on NFHS Network all year Streetsboro 28, Tallmadge 14 The Rockets won a back-and-forth thriller and got some help from Norton to earn a share of the Metro Athletic Conference championship. The Rockets needed the Panthers to win at Cloverleaf and needed to win their own game at Tallmadge to earn a share of the title. Norton ended up beating Cloverleaf 42-7, but the action in Tallmadge was far closer. Dallas Morris had an 83-yard punt return and Logan Sadowski added a 43-yard field goal to give Streetsboro a 10-0 lead with four minutes and change remaining until halftime. The Blue Devils responded with a touchdown before halftime and added another roughly five minutes into the second half to take a 14-10 lead. Sadowski added another long field goal, this time from 42 yards out, in the third quarter to draw the Rockets within a point, and Colton Cox took care of the rest. The senior quarterback's 6-yard touchdown run and an ensuing two-point conversion gave the Rockets the lead with 9:48 remaining. His 27-yard touchdown toss to Kyle Giacomo clinched the game. Meanwhile, Logan Fincham easily eclipsed the century mark running the football for Streetsboro (8-2, 6-1). The Rockets will share the 2026 MAC title with the Panthers, who they beat by a touchdown, and the Colts, who they lost to by a touchdown. A three-way tie isn't new to the Metro. In fact, Cloverleaf, Norton and Woodridge tied for the championship in 2022. With its win at Tallmadge, Streetsboro clinched the top seed in Region 13 and will not play again until Week 12. Mogadore 28, Brush 22 The Wildcats outscored the Arcs 21-0 in the fourth quarter to cap a stunning comeback and clinch a first-round bye. Down 22-0, Maddox Smith got Mogadore on the scoreboard with a 9-yard touchdown run to end the third quarter. Smith added an 11-yard touchdown pass to Collin Hendrickson to make it 22-13 early in the fourth quarter, and Kade Thomas tallied two 2-yard touchdown runs to complete the comeback. Thomas turned a game-high 30 carries into 98 yards for the Wildcats (8-2). Smith added a game-high 106 rushing yards on 23 carries. Smith also completed 9 of 18 passes for 157 yards, with Hendrickson (five catches, 105 yards) serving as his leading receiver. Down 14-0, Brookfield pulled within a score. Down 21-7, the Warriors responded with another touchdown. Ryder Cain had the first two touchdowns for Garfield while Nate Baczkowski had the final score for the G-Men (10-0, 7-0). Garfield thus clinched

Knotted 14-14 at the end of 36 minutes, the teams combined for 24 points in a wild fourth quarter. Matthew Panzner started the craziness with a 34-yard field goal to give Copley a 17-14 lead. Aurora answered with a 45-yard touchdown run by Carter Fitzgerald to go ahead 20-17. Copley responded with an even longer touchdown — a 74-yard pass from Dane Wininger to Noah Slattery — to take a 24-20 lead with 2:50 remaining. But the Greenmen answered with a 9-yard touchdown run by McGovern, who also had a 90-yard kick return touchdown for Aurora (5-5, 4-3 Suburban American), which finished the season on a three-game win streak. Slattery had four catches for 121 yards and two scores, serving as a leading receiver for Wininger (10-of-17 passing, 204 yards, two TDs, 2 INTs). Wininger also ran for 109 yards on 15 carries and Jalen Owens added 94 yards on 14 carries for Copley (6-4, 3-4). Fitzgerald turned 22 carries into 141 yards and two touchdowns for Aurora, while Marc McGovern completed 12 of 19 passes for 123 yards. Luke Hilditch and Luke McGovern added an interception apiece for the Greenmen. Other area scores: Chagrin Falls 24, Crestwood 21 Memorial 22, Waterloo 6 Liberty 41, Southeast 7 Contact Jonah L. item.title: Chiefs star Kenneth Walker III reacts to Jalen Hurts’ blood clot ordeal
item.description: Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has sent a message of support to Jalen Hurts after the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback was diagnosed with blood clots that will keep him out for the rest of the regular season. Walker knows how serious the situation can be, having suffered a pulmonary embolism involving blood clots in both lungs during his high school years. Hurts’ diagnosis has raised concerns over how the Eagles handled his condition after he played against the Jacksonville Jaguars despite initially being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his calf. Kenneth Walker III urges Jalen Hurts to focus on recovery Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot ahead of Philadelphia’s game against Jacksonville in London. The Eagles’ medical staff determined he was fit to play, but he was reportedly instructed not to sleep the night before the game, leaving him awake for 36 consecutive hours before taking the field. The situation became more serious when it emerged that the blood clots had spread to Hurts’ lungs. He was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the regular season as he began his recovery. Walker was shocked by the circumstances surrounding Hurts’ appearance against Jacksonville. Speaking to reporters, the Chiefs running back reacted to the quarterback’s travel and playing arrangements before offering words of encouragement. Walker said: “He went on the flight, huh? And everything? Yeah, that’s crazy.” He then shared a message for the Eagles star: “Just stay positive. Do all the things necessary that you need to do to get your body back right. I’ll be praying for him, because that’s not something we should take lightly.” Walker’s own experience helps explain why he stressed the importance of taking the diagnosis seriously. Blood clots can pose significant health risks, and the running back has dealt with a similar medical emergency himself. Hurts is now taking blood thinners as he works towards a full recovery. Philadelphia must also find a way to compete without its starting quarterback for the remainder of the regular season. The Eagles have struggled recently and are looking to end a four-game losing streak against the Dallas Cowboys. However, Hurts’ health remains the priority after a worrying episode that has drawn scrutiny towards the team’s handling of his condition. For Walker, the message was clear: Hurts must focus on his recovery and avoid taking unnecessary risks with his health. item.title: Friday Seacoast Roundup: STA field hockey, Marshwood boys soccer advance, more results
item.description: DOVER — Riley Thomas scored a goal and added an assist as the fourth-seeded St. Thomas Aquinas field hockey team beat No. 5 Plymouth, 2-1 on Friday in a Division II quarterfinal. "This season, we've learned to adapt as a team and I think that helped us today," St. Thomas head coach Lindsay Dobecki said. "As a coaching staff, we're really proud of the effort from everyone and, of course, the outcome. This team has worked so hard to get to this point and it showed today." St. Thomas will now play No. 1 Souhegan in a semifinal on Tuesday, Oct. 27 at Exeter High School. Game time is scheduled for 7 p.m. "We're excited to be able to move on to the semifinals and look forward to continuing to make improvements as a team," Dobecki said. The other semifinal features No. 2 Bow and No. 3 Hanover. Bow advanced with a 5-0 win over No. 10 Oyster River. Thomas opened the scoring with 3:41 remaining in the first quarter. After Plymouth tied the game, Leah Walsh netted the game-winner with 3:26 left in regulation. "The win today was overall just a great team effort," Dobecki said. "We had so many players step up in big ways to help set up plays. What really stood out was the way everyone supported each other on the field and moved as a unit." FIELD HOCKEY No. 7 Windham 4 No. 10 Marshwood 2 WINDHAM, Maine — Hazel Stout scored one goal and assisted on Ellie Adams', but the Hawks saw their season come to an end with this Class A preliminary round loss. Windham jumped out to a 4-0 lead with two goals in the first quarter, and one in both the second and third quarters. "Today was a full team effort to come back and keep sparking in a challenging season," Marshwood head coach Molly Humiston said. "We're very proud of the effort and growth this team showed throughout the season." BOYS SOCCER No. 9 Marshwood 1 No. 8 Kennebunk 0, 2OT KENNEBUNK, Maine - The ninth-seeded Hawks defeated No. 8 Kennebunk in penalty shots, 4-3, after two scoreless overtimes in a Class A South preliminary round game. Marshwood's penalty-kick scorers were Kyler DeWildt, Finn Parker, Julian Scott and Chad Anderson, whose successful attempt clinched a 4-3 victory in the shootout. Marshwood (7-5-3) will visit top-seeded Thornton Academy on Tuesday in a quarterfinal round game. "Our identity all season has just been toughness and defense," said Marshwood coach Ben Deschenes. "It keeps us in games even when we're having a hard time scoring. I think tonight that was the case again." Goalkeeper Jack Eardley made four saves to help keep the Rams off the scoreboard through regulation and overtime. "Hopefully we can connect on more of our set pieces against Thornton Academy," Deschenes said. VOLLEYBALL Dover 3 Merrimack 1 DOVER — Jovie Meeker had 27 digs, including the 500th of her career in this Division I match for Dover, which ended its Division I regular season with a record of 9-9. Avery Flynn had 29 assists and three aces for the Green Wave, and Ayla Raynor had eight kills, 15 digs and three aces. S

item.title: Chelsea fans’ preferred lineup against Spurs: Never change a winning lineup
item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 17: Pedro Neto of Chelsea celebrates after scoring a goal to make it 0-2 during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Everton and Chelsea FC at Hill Dickinson Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Liverpool, United Kingdom. (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images) | Getty Images Xabi Alonso made just one change last weekend from the prior game, and that one change was enforced by injury. Pep Chavarría was not able to go, so Jorrel Hato had to step in. That decision paid off, both in terms of Hato contributing with an assist and in terms of Chelsea winning back-to-back matches: 5-1 against AFC Bournemouth and then 2-0 against Everton. Can that lineup make it three for three? The WAGNH Community certainly believe so, voting in the same starting lineup, with every starter reaching over three-quarters majority and most of them garnering over 90 per cent of the vote. There is one change, obviously, at starting goalkeeper as Mike Penders is forced to step in for Emiliano Martínez, who’s recovering from surgery on is fractured jaw. 3-4-3 / 3-4-2-1 (68%) Penders (98%) | Colwill (95%), Lacroix (98%), Acheampong (93%) | Hato (76%), Henderson (87%), Caicedo (99%), Neto (89%) | Rogers (98%), Palmer (99%) | João Pedro (98%) Marco Palestra (27%), Roméo Lavia (12%), and Estêvão (11%) were the only other players to get into the double-digits.

item.title: Titans’ Robert Saleh gets real about Alontae Taylor position change ahead of Browns matchup
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Titans’ Robert Saleh gets real about Alontae Taylor position change ahead of Browns matchup appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh is shaking things up in the secondary ahead of a crucial home matchup against the Cleveland Browns . Cornerback Alontae Taylor, who joined the franchise on a big three-year contract this past offseason, was a surprising healthy scratch during Tennessee’s 26-20 road victory over the Indianapolis Colts. However, Saleh revealed that the defensive coaching staff is re-evaluating his role by actively working him into slot rotations during practice this week. “We’ve gotten him some nickel reps trying to get this close, he’s attacked the heck out of it, he acknowledges it too, our nickel is a lot different,” Saleh said. “You know, he played both nickel and corner and I’ve always been a big firm believer that he can play just one position let’s see how good he can get but at the end of the day he got here because of his ability to play now and we felt like he could still go play corner but at the same time, it was just a ‘what is his fastball?’ And I suppose we’ve really got to recognize what his fastball is.” #Titans Robert Saleh acknowledged Alontae Taylor was initially going to play only corner but they're going to get him some reps at nickel. Saleh likes how Taylor bounced back and it started with his energy during the game even though he was inactive. pic.twitter.com/IKqcGnV8hI Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — TURRON DAVENPORT (@TDavenport_NFL) October 23, 2026 Saleh praised how Taylor responded to the benching , highlighting his high energy and enthusiasm on the sideline despite being inactive. Shifting him back inside is a noteworthy pivot for the scheme. Taylor is widely considered at his absolute best as a disruptive slot defender, whereas his outside transition produced mixed results. Through his first five starts this year, opposing quarterbacks completed 21 of 24 pass attempts thrown in his direction. Tennessee’s defense showed real teeth against Indianapolis in his absence, racking up six sacks and grabbing two interceptions off quarterback Daniel Jones. As the Titans prepare to defend home turf against Cleveland, unleashing Taylor’s “fastball” in the slot could give the secondary the exact playmaker energy it needs to stack back-to-back wins this season. Related: 7 teams that must sell at 2026 NFL trade deadline, and the players who should be on move Related: Titans’ Alontae Taylor sends defiant social media message after benching sparks trade rumors

Saleh likes how Taylor bounced back and it started with his energy during the game even though he was inactive. pic.twitter.com/IKqcGnV8hI Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — TURRON DAVENPORT (@TDavenport_NFL) October 23, 2026 Saleh praised how Taylor responded to the benching , highlighting his high energy and enthusiasm on the sideline despite being inactive. Shifting him back inside is a noteworthy pivot for the scheme. Taylor is widely considered at his absolute best as a disruptive slot defender, whereas his outside transition produced mixed results. Through his first five starts this year, opposing quarterbacks completed 21 of 24 pass attempts thrown in his direction. Tennessee’s defense showed real teeth against Indianapolis in his absence, racking up six sacks and grabbing two interceptions off quarterback Daniel Jones. As the Titans prepare to defend home turf against Cleveland, unleashing Taylor’s “fastball” in the slot could give the secondary the exact playmaker energy it needs to stack back-to-back wins this season. item.title: San Juan Hills pulls off upset of San Clemente with a shutout
item.description: San Juan Hills High defensive back Arthur Tuverson had a pick-six to clinch a win over San Clemente on Friday night. (Caleb Otte / For The Times) The energy at The Badlands Stadium on Friday night was too much for Mother Earth to handle. She had to put a temporary stop to it. Both sets of players for San Juan Hills High and San Clemente were fired up by a full crowd of rowdy fans, and it promised to be one of the best high school atmospheres of the season. But then everybody was forced into the basketball gym after five minutes and seven seconds of play. For 90 minutes a lightning delay threatened to end the affair all together. Nothing, however, could force these two teams and communities to give up on this night. After the Norte fire tore through 570 acres across south Orange County, destroying many homes in the process, everybody needed this. The matchup — which hadn’t been played since 2021 — meant so much to both the Stallions and Tritons. “Between the white lines, for 48 minutes, I expect nothing less than war,” San Juan Hills head coach Robert Frith said before kickoff. It was San Juan Hills (8-1) that ultimately came through with an 16-0 upset victory, which puts it on the brink of the Alpha League title before next week’s big matchup against Mission Viejo. This was the Stallions’ first win against San Clemente (7-1) since 2015, and likely knocked the Tritons out of contention for the CIF Southern Section Division 1 playoffs. That felt pretty sweet for Arthur Tuverson, who gave a little smack talk to the San Clemente student section after the game, taunting them about the defense’s shutout. It was the junior defensive back’s 52-yard touchdown interception that sealed the victory. As he ran it down the field, the noise in the stadium reached pre-delay levels. “I knew they were in desperation mode and needed to pass the ball,” Tuverson said after the win. “I made the play. I was waiting for it.” Both teams played with backup quarterbacks as Preston Beck for San Clemente and Eiler King for San Juan Hills were out because of injuries. The Stallions turned to senior Parker Armstrong, who started two years at Scripps Ranch High in San Diego. He finished the night completing 17 for 19 passes for 172 yards, doing enough to manage a low scoring contest and help his team not turn the ball over for the seventh game running. That felt pretty sweet for Arthur Tuverson, who gave a little smack talk to the San Clemente student section after the game, taunting them about the defense’s shutout. I was waiting for it.” Both teams played with backup quarterbacks as Preston Beck for San Clemente and Eiler King for San Juan Hills were out because of injuries. The Stallions turned to senior Parker Armstrong, who started two years at Scripps Ranch High in San Diego. The Tritons gave freshman Koston James his first taste of varsity action, but it was a tough game to come into as he finished 11-for-16 passing for 60 yards with two interceptions. San Clemente coach Jaime Ortiz knew that points would be at a premium in this matchup. “We’re going to have to play good defense and not allow the big play,” Ortiz said pregame. Frith called it a power of wills. San Clemente let gave up only 20 rushing yards, but San Juan Hills’ two interceptions and swarming defensive line swung the game. Late in the third quarter, San Clemente attempted a flea flicker and San Juan Hills was on James the second he got the ball back. It was exemplary of the home team’s sustained energy during a long and tiring night. San Clemente often ran two-way star Jaxson Rex out of the Wildcat formation, letting the Brigham Young commit’s athleticism take center stage. A lot was put on the talented senior’s shoulders to get the offense going. He finished with five catches for 42 yards and 32 rushing yards. His counterpart, Texas State commit Luke Frith, finished with four catches for 48 yards. Frith noted pregame that special teams would have a big role to play in the night. He was correct, as San Juan Hills senior kicker Trevor Koko knocked through two field goals in the first half, and then nailed a season-long 44-yarder to put the Stallions up 9-0 in the third quarter. San Clemente missed a field goal when down 3-0. Penalties also hurt the Tritons as they committed 10 for 105 yards in the team’s first loss of the season after last week’s game against Mission Viejo was cancelled because of the Norte fire. Before the game, first responders were honored and both coaches made sure to express their gratitude for the swift and effective work of those who protected the communities. The coaches on both sidelines wore Orange County Fire Authority hats as a token of gratitude. “[The hats] are a sign that it is sometimes bigger than football, and a lot of programs could take note of that,” Ortiz said. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

item.title: "I hope that one day I can play at his level" – Maza reacts to Wirtz comparisons
item.description: "I hope that one day I can play at his level" – Maza reacts to Wirtz comparisons Following his €12 million move from Hertha BSC to Bayer Leverkusen last year, Ibrahim Maza was quickly touted as a potential successor to Florian Wirtz, who left the club to join Liverpool in a big-money move that summer. In a recent interview with the DFL, the 20-year-old attacking midfielder revealed how he deals with the comparisons to Wirtz, who was a major star in Leverkusen's domestic double winning campaign. “I don't know. It is still the same, of course. Flo is an incredible player, a real Leverkusen legend and everything," Maza said, adding: "I am still trying to follow my own path and be my own player. I think we are a little different in terms of our playing styles, but of course, it is nice to be able to follow in the footsteps of such a great player. I hope that one day I can play at his level and achieve that.” Despite being just 20, Maza has established himself as a key player in attacking midfield for Die Werkself. “It does make me proud, of course, that I can take on that kind of responsibility for such a big club. At the same time, I try to block it out and simply focus on what happens on the pitch, keep doing my own thing, and enjoy playing," he said. In the interview, the Algeria international was also asked about his role models, naming former Arsenal and Germany midfielder Mesut Özil and ex-Chelsea and Belgium winger Eden Hazard. “When I was young, I loved Mesut Özil and Eden Hazard. Those two were incredible for me. I loved watching the way they played football. Nowadays, it is difficult to name one role model when you suddenly play against everyone. I try to learn a little from everyone and take the best from each person, including my teammates," he explained.

Round 1 (Browns) - #26 KJ Duff, WR (Rutgers) I will be honest, I'm not entirely wowed with this range of the draft. Round 2 (Browns) - #58 Damon Wilson, ED (Miami) I really wish Clev Lubin the edge out of Louisville was younger. There are several choices here but I go with Wilson who is a pass rushing monster. The run stuffing needs work, but I want to add a wrecking machine to cause defenses more issues. Round 3 (Browns) - #90 Anthony Boswell, C (Houston) The Cleveland Browns have four starters on the offensive line next season, the one question based on contract is Jenkins. I would select Boswell here and have a year to develop him. With Jenkins' versatility, they can move him along the line if there is an injury.

item.title: John Murtough: Controversial former Man United chief lands new role in English football
item.description: John Murtough: Controversial former Man United chief lands new role in English football Former Manchester United football director John Murtough has landed a new role at Birmingham City. United career Murtough started working at United in 2013 after previously working with David Moyes at Everton. He began his role as head of football development in 2016 and eventually worked his way up to football director in 2020. Murtough was active during the reigns of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag but had left before the Dutchman was sacked in October 2024. The director was a controversial figure during his time at the club and is associated with such deals as the Antony, Jadon Sancho, Rasmus Hojlund and Mason Mount transfers, which cost millions of pounds for very little reward for the club. New role Nonetheless, Murtough has secured a new position in English football at Birmingham City. The BBC reports that, “Birmingham City have appointed former Manchester United chief John Murtough as their new director of football. Murtough, 55, who left United in April 2024 as football director after 11 years at Old Trafford, becomes the replacement for Craig Gardner, who departed St Andrew’s in June.” His most recent role was that of director of global development at Atalanta. It is also stated that Birmingham boss Chris Davies “will report into Murtough, while his remit also covers recruitment, data, performance and the pathway from the academy into the first team.” Murtough will also “collaborate with Hope Powell to ensure that the Blues women’s team, enjoy ‘continued development benefits from the club’s wider football strategy’.” Commenting on his new position, the former United employee stated, “this is a great football club with brilliant fans and enormous potential. There is a clear determination from Knighthead to build something special for the long term, both on and off the pitch.” The Blues currently sit fourth in the Championship, eyeing promotion to the Premier League. Featured image by Michael Regan via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Barcelona vs Real Madrid preview: Catalan giants look to bounce back from PSG nightmare against Los Blancos
item.description: Barcelona vs Real Madrid preview: Catalan giants look to bounce back from PSG nightmare against Los Blancos Barcelona will look to protect their perfect La Liga record when they host Real Madrid in El Clasico on Sunday, October 25. Hansi Flick’s side have won all nine league matches, but face a Madrid team desperate to close the six-point gap at the summit. Barcelona vs Real Madrid – Head-to-Head record Barcelona and Real Madrid have met 264 times, with both sides recording 106 wins and 52 draws . In La Liga, Madrid lead with 80 victories to Barcelona’s 77, alongside 35 draws. Barcelona have won six of their last seven meetings with Madrid, including a 2-0 victory in last season’s corresponding league fixture. Barcelona – Flick’s unbeaten league leaders face a test Barcelona have won their opening nine La Liga matches, collecting 27 points and sitting five points above second-placed Atletico Madrid. They beat Real Betis 5-2 before suffering a 4-2 Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain. Lamine Yamal has registered 10 goals and 10 assists in 12 appearances this term, making him a major threat. Dani Olmo and Eric Garcia are ruled out through injury, while Jules Kounde is a doubt. Barcelona will need to manage their defensive absences carefully against Kylian Mbappe. Probable line-up for Barcelona (4-2-3-1) Joan Garcia; Joao Cancelo, Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin, Xavi Espart; Rodri, Pedri; Lamine Yamal, Fermin Lopez, Anthony Gordon; Raphinha. Real Madrid – Jose Mourinho’s side aim to cut the gap Real Madrid have won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their defeat to Atletico Madrid, beating Villarreal, Roma, Sevilla and RB Leipzig. Their latest result was a convincing 4-1 Champions League victory over Leipzig, following an identical scoreline against Sevilla. Los Blancos sit third in La Liga on 21 points and cannot afford another setback if they want to keep pace with Barcelona. Rodrygo, Ferland Mendy and Raul Asencio are unavailable through injury, while Vinicius Junior is suspended . Mbappe will lead Jose Mourinho’s attack. Probable line-up for Real Madrid (4-2-3-1) Thibaut Courtois; Federico Valverde, Ibrahima Konate, Dean Huijsen, Marc Cucurella; Aurelien Tchouameni, Bernardo Silva; Arda Guler, Jude Bellingham, Yan Diomande; Kylian Mbappe. item.title: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum Sounds Off in Lengthy NSFW Rant About Ex-Teammate Jaylen Brown

(Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - APRIL 05: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Boston Celtics (left) and Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics embrace during introductions prior to a game against the Toronto Raptors at TD Garden on April 05, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) Getty The Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum has plenty to say about the conversation surrounding his relationship with former teammate Jaylen Brown. After Brown responded with a cap emoji beneath a video about his trade to Philadelphia, Tatum addressed the speculation directly. His response included a pointed reminder that their years together deserve more than becoming material for an internet argument. Tatum said he has no animosity toward Brown and would welcome a conversation with him. He also described reaching out after the trade, while acknowledging that people process major changes differently. What clearly bothers him is how quickly the discussion has shifted from their shared success to questions about their personal relationship. For Celtics fans, that distinction matters. Tatum and Brown spent years hearing doubts about whether their partnership could deliver a championship before eventually answering them. Their separation does not erase that accomplishment, even if the latest social media exchange has drawn attention elsewhere. Celtics’ Jayson Tatum Addresses Jaylen Brown’s Cap Emoji Brown’s reaction appeared beneath a video in which Tatum recalled finding out about the trade that sent his longtime teammate to the 76ers. The blue cap emoji commonly signals that someone is “capping,” slang for lying. Brown appeared to dispute Tatum’s account, although he did not specify which detail he questioned. Tatum’s response went beyond defending a particular part of that story. He focused on the broader treatment of their relationship and the suggestion that their separation had become a personal feud. His frustration centered on what he believes is getting lost. “I understand we are in an entertainment business, but me personally, I am not much of an off-the-court entertainer type of guy,” Tatum said, via video shared by Daniel Donabedian . “For me, it’s just like, I don’t have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him. The frustrating part is since he’s not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or the conversations haven’t been enough about what we accomplished, all the games we won, winning the championship, how we’ve grown together. Right, it’s turned into this like drama type of thing.” There is a fair point inside that frustration. Their partnership produced far more than a collection of moments for fans to dissect after the breakup. Reducing the entire relationship to whether one player believes the other’s trade story leaves out what made their time together significant. Celtics Star Says a Conversation Could Clear the Air Tatum also offered his account of trying to contact Brown after the deal. His comments do not establish Brown’s perspective or explain the motivation behind the emoji. They do make clear that Tatum says he has been willing to communicate. “I got two kids, you know what I’m saying? I reached out to him the day he got traded. I called him, I texted him, and I understand people process things differently,” Tatum said. “So for me, like at this point in our lives, we are too old to be having our relationship discussed, X, Y, Z, on the internet. There’s a conversation to be had. We can definitely have that conversation. I welcome that.” “I have always wanted the best for him and wished the best for him. I always publicly said those things. I seen all these things about ‘get your popcorn ready’ when they play. There’s no f***ing boxing match. Again, there’s no animosity, there’s no beef. I just hate the way the conversation and narrative around it. There’s not enough communication. I think a conversation would solve and put out a lot of fires.” The boxing reference captured how far Tatum believes the buildup has gone. Boston and Philadelphia already have enough competitive stakes without every meeting becoming a referendum on whether two former teammates still like each other. Tatum is explicitly rejecting the idea that he views Brown as a personal enemy. Getty BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS – APRIL 05: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Boston Celtics (left) and Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics embrace during introductions prior to a game against the Toronto Raptors at TD Garden on April 05, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) That does not mean every question has been answered. Brown’s emoji remains open to interpretation beyond its general expression of disbelief, and Tatum’s response does not resolve the apparent disagreement. A direct conversation would offer a better opportunity for clarity than another round of online speculation. For now, Celtics fans have a clear statement from their star. Tatum wants their accomplishments remembered, says there is no beef and has left the door open to talk. Whether that produces a resolution is uncertain, but their championship partnership deserves more consideration than a single emoji can provide. item.title: Harsha Bhogle slams India's 'bland, heartless' pitches after Dhruv Jurel-led IND-A collapses in New Zealand
item.description: Harsha Bhogle slams India's 'bland, heartless' pitches after Dhruv Jurel-led IND-A collapses in New Zealand originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India A were dismissed for just 113 against New Zealand A on a lively Lincoln pitch, with several Test regulars failing. New Zealand A openers Rhys Mariu and Curtis Heaphy put on 131 before the Indian seamers finally struck back late in the day. Harsha Bhogle argued that the collapse shows why Indian batters need exposure to varied surfaces rather than the flat tracks made for T20 cricket. India A 113 all out: Harsha Bhogle reacts to New Zealand collapse, questions pitch preparation back at home Harsha Bhogle has strongly criticised the “bland, heartless” pitches used in Indian cricket after a star-studded India A batting line-up folded for 113 on a testing opening day in Lincoln. The first four-day unofficial Test against New Zealand A on Saturday was meant to be a useful warm-up for the senior players, but it turned into a harsh reminder of how demanding conditions in the country can be. India’s top order carried plenty of Test experience into this contest, yet almost none of it counted for much on a surface that offered help to the bowlers. Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan and captain Dhruv Jurel all found run-scoring difficult, and the side was bowled out in only 39.3 overs. The home team then reached 135/3 in 41 overs by the close of play, leaving the visitors well behind in the contest. The toss had already worked in the hosts’ favour. Mariu chose to field, having read the bowling-friendly conditions correctly, and Rahul fell for a duck to the seamer Fraser Sheat before the innings had settled. Jaiswal then tried to hold one end together alongside Padikkal, who came in at No.3, but Zak Gibson removed him for 17 off 45 balls. item.content:encoded: Harsha Bhogle slams India's 'bland, heartless' pitches after Dhruv Jurel-led IND-A collapses in New Zealand originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India A were dismissed for just 113 against New Zealand A on a lively Lincoln pitch, with several Test regulars failing. New Zealand A openers Rhys Mariu and Curtis Heaphy put on 131 before the Indian seamers finally struck back late in the day. Harsha Bhogle argued that the collapse shows why Indian batters need exposure to varied surfaces rather than the flat tracks made for T20 cricket. India A 113 all out: Harsha Bhogle reacts to New Zealand collapse, questions pitch preparation back at home Harsha Bhogle has strongly criticised the “bland, heartless” pitches used in Indian cricket after a star-studded India A batting line-up folded for 113 on a testing opening day in Lincoln. The first four-day unofficial Test against New Zealand A on Saturday was meant to be a useful warm-up for the senior players, but it turned into a harsh reminder of how demanding conditions in the country can be. India’s top order carried plenty of Test experience into this contest, yet almost none of it counted for much on a surface that offered help to the bowlers. Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan and captain Dhruv Jurel all found run-scoring difficult, and the side was bowled out in only 39.3 overs. The home team then reached 135/3 in 41 overs by the close of play, leaving the visitors well behind in the contest. The toss had already worked in the hosts’ favour. Mariu chose to field, having read the bowling-friendly conditions correctly, and Rahul fell for a duck to the seamer Fraser Sheat before the innings had settled. Jaiswal then tried to hold one end together alongside Padikkal, who came in at No.3, but Zak Gibson removed him for 17 off 45 balls. India A fully up against it in their warm up match prior the Test Series in New Zealand They sit at 54/4 with some great bowling by Keene to dismiss the Indian Batsman Padikkal the only player to really get going for India currently 32* off 75 balls A sign of things to come for India in the upcoming weeks? — JN Sport (@JNSports1) October 24, 2026 The most damaging spell came from the right-arm pacer Simon Keene, who finished with figures of 5/24. Sudharsan, who is competing with Padikkal for the No.3 position in the Test side, was bowled by him without scoring. Jurel followed soon after as Keene’s second victim, and the wicketkeeper-batter managed only a single run, which left the visiting captain with little to build on. Padikkal was the one batter who looked comfortable, and he seemed set for a substantial score before Gibson returned to dismiss him for 32 off 77 balls, an innings that included five boundaries. Things could have looked a lot worse but for Yash Rathod, who came in at No.6 and played freely for an unbeaten 44 from 49 balls. He struck three fours and three sixes, and his lower-order counterparts did not offer much support, since Washington Sundar and Akash Deep were both dismissed for ducks and Anshul Kamboj added 10. Rathod’s effort was largely the reason the total crossed the 100 mark. (getty) Indian seamers struggle as Rhys Mariu and Curtis Heaphy build a 131-run opening stand The bowlers were expected to respond strongly, and the group of Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj, Mukesh Choudhary and Aquib Nabi had a chance to show what they could do on the same surface. For a long time, however, they could not make a dent. Mariu and Heaphy batted with confidence and put together 131 for the first wicket, which left India A with a deficit they could hardly have imagined at the start. Mariu looked on course for a hundred before Choudhary trapped him leg before for 76. Nabi then struck twice in successive deliveries, and both dismissals were leg-before decisions, which gave the visitors a brief lift. Heaphy, on 37, and Matthew Boyle, on 0, were the not-out batters when stumps were called. MORE: 'No reply to this day': Amit Mishra reveals shocking cold shoulder from Virat Kohli after 2017 comeback snub 'Pitches don't test batters at home': Harsha Bhogle weighs in on India A's 113-run collapse against New Zealand A Veteran commentator Harsha Bhogle felt the result said less about the individual batters and more about the surfaces on which they usually play. He wrote on X: "A very good India A side bowled out for 113 and a good bowling line-up being countered easily by New Zealand A. The very reason why home and away cricket is important and why you must learn to play on different surfaces rather than on the same, bland, heartless pitches we think are good for T20 cricket.” A very good India A side bowled out for 113 and a good bowling line-up being countered easily by New Zealand A. The very reason why home and away cricket is important and why you must learn to play on different surfaces rather than on the same, bland, heartless pitches we think are good for T20 cricket. — Harsha Bhogle (@bhogleharsha) October 24, 2026 India A will play two more unofficial Tests on this tour, and the squad will use them to get valuable practice and adjust to the conditions. The senior team’s two-Test series begins on November 19 at Wellington, so the time available for the Test-squad members to find some rhythm is not long. India A collapse sends an early warning sign to Gautam Gambhir & Co. Rahul, Jaiswal, Sudharsan and Padikkal are all in the conversation for Test spots. They have now seen how quickly a good-looking batting order can come apart when the ball seams and bounces. That is a lesson best learned in Lincoln and not in Wellington. Bhogle’s wider point is also hard to argue with. Indian domestic and white-ball cricket has leaned heavily on pitches that reward stroke-play and give bowlers little to work with, and batters raised on those tracks often need time to rebuild their defence overseas. The same applies to bowlers, who found nothing special in the conditions for a long stretch of the afternoon. item.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
item.description: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico. Not yet anyway, but it’s time: on Sunday night he returns to the stadium he first arrived at 30 transformative years ago as Bobby Robson’s talented young translator, and last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football. The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too. Continue reading...

item.title: Wales great Faletau suffers fresh injury blow
item.description: Taulupe Faletau made his Wales debut in 2011 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau has been sidelined again after an injury blow on his Cardiff comeback. The 35-year-old made his first appearance since March in the Champions Cup defeat by Northampton on 18 October. He made an accomplished return but reported finger pain in the days afterwards and will have surgery. Faletau will miss the United Rugby Championship (URC) derby at Ospreys that finishes the first block of the season. It is hoped he will be fit to return after the November break for the Nations Championship. "Unfortunately he had a little bit of a niggle with a pinkie finger, so he will be on the sidelines for a while," said Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl. "He will miss the Ospreys game but hopefully after November he will be fine." Wales great Faletau still has drive for fourth World Cup Six-try Sharks condemn Cardiff to rare home defeat Faletau has played only 31 times for Cardiff since joining from Bath in 2022 and was limited to seven appearances last season because of shoulder, calf and knee injuries. "I can imagine he is quite frustrated because after the game he didn't even realise it, then the next day it was sore all of a sudden," said Van Zyl. "It's a tough one for him to take, but hopefully he can turn it around." Faletau's lack of game-time meant he was not included in Wales' squad for the Nations Championship, with in-form Cardiff team-mate Taine Basham getting a recall instead. Wales head coach Steve Tandy said they would not rule out an international return for Faletau, who has won 109 caps and played at three World Cups, but that he needed to show durability to go along with his undoubted quality. The latest blow only adds to those fears about the legendary number eight, who signed a one-year contract extension with Cardiff last summer. Cardiff will not only be without Faletau against Ospreys on Saturday, 31 October but their Wales back-row forwards Alex Mann, James Botham and Basham. They will hope that number eight Alun Lawrence, who has not featured this season because of a number of niggles, will be fit for the trip to Swansea. Dan Thomas, summer signing Semisi Paea and youngster Lucas de la Rua have played in the back row this season, with hooker Evan Lloyd another option. Cardiff suffered a third successive loss when beaten by Sharks at the Arms Park on Friday.

item.title: How Rodri and Raphinha fired up the Barcelona dressing room after PSG loss
item.description: How Rodri and Raphinha fired up the Barcelona dressing room after PSG loss Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the season in midweek as they lost 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. For a side that has been dominating every single game this season, the defeat raised more questions than it should have. But fortunately for Barcelona, the team has two great leaders in the team, who were quick to rally up the troops by giving impassioned ‘lessons’ to their teammates after the PSG loss. Rodri and Raphinha’s message to the team Raphinha has emerged as a real leader at Barcelona. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) As reported by Diario SPORT , the Barcelona dressing room has emerged from the defeat with its spirits intact, and two senior figures played a key role in setting the tone. Shortly after the game, it was captain Raphinha who first addressed the group, delivering a talk aimed at drawing the right conclusions and lessons from the loss. Rodri, who will be playing his first El Clasico this weekend, then followed. The Spaniard stressed that if mistakes are going to be made, this early stage of the season is precisely the time to make them and learn. The Ballon d’Or winner spoke with particular energy about the demands of the biggest occasions, emphasising that in matches against the best teams in the world, concentration and decision-making in every single play are what separate winning from losing. The sentiment was shared by Flick’s coaching staff and the squad’s veterans, who agreed the game was lost through poor decision-making at key moments rather than any deeper woe. The report adds that the group remains united and confident that, by eliminating those specific errors, they can still compete for every trophy on offer. Why both will be crucial against Real Madrid Rodri is expected to start vs Real Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) It goes without saying that both Raphinha and Rodri will play a crucial role once again as Barcelona take on Real Madrid on Sunday. Rodri, who started the PSG game on the bench as Flick managed his workload, is expected to return to the heart of midfield for the Clasico . His calm, control and big-game experience, exactly the qualities he preached to his teammates, could prove invaluable against a Real Madrid side desperate to disrupt Barça’s rhythm. Raphinha, meanwhile, will be eager to lead by example after a rare off night in Paris. The captain was well below his usual standards against PSG, and few occasions offer a better stage for redemption than a Clasico at the Camp Nou.
