item.title: How will Barcelona line up against Real Madrid?
item.description: Photo By Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images Barcelona look to bounce back from their first defeat of the season and make it 10 wins out of 10 in La Liga when they welcome Real Madrid to Camp Nou for the first El Clásico of the campaign. Here’s how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Sunday’s battle: Defense Flick is still dealing with a defensive injury crisis as Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen have been ruled out through injury and Jules Kounde is unlikely to feature with an ankle issue. The absences mean the starting back four will be the same as we saw in Paris, with Xavi Espart at right-back despite a minor ankle issue, Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín at center-back, and João Cancelo ahead of Alejandro Balde at left-back. Midfield Dani Olmo is out for the next month through injury and Gavi and Frenkie de Jong are unlikely to start this one, so the regular midfield three of Rodri , Pedri and Fermín López will be chosen to face Los Blancos . Attack Captain Raphinha looked a little rusty on his return from injury but was able to play an hour in Paris and should be good to go from the start in this one, with Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon completing the front three on Sunday. Possible XI : Joan; Espart, Cubarsí, Martín, Cancelo; Fermín, Rodri, Pedri; Yamal, Raphinha, Gordon (4-3-3) How do you think Barcelona should line up against Real Madrid? Let us know your thoughts, predictions and teams in the comments below!

item.title: ‘He Made It Look Easy’ – Jonathan Di Bella Salutes Jonathan Haggerty’s Fierce Finish At ONE SAMURAI 4
item.description: Jonathan “The General” Haggerty did not just keep his crown in Tokyo. He gave kickboxing fans a performance to remember, and ONE Strawweight Kickboxing World Champion Jonathan Di Bella was among those impressed. The ONE Bantamweight Kickboxing World Champion smashed his way to a third-round finish against former titleholder Hiroki Akimoto in their ONE SAMURAI 4 main event showdown inside Ariake Arena on Saturday, October 17. Photo Credit: ONE Championship With the triumph, the 29-year-old Londoner improved to 25-5 overall, stayed perfect at 4-0 in kickboxing, and earned a US$100,000 performance bonus from ONE Chairman and CEO Chatri Sityodtong. A finish like that gets a World Champion’s attention. The Italian-Canadian expected Haggerty to come through in “The Land of the Rising Sun,” but he least expected it to end in that fashion. Di Bella told onefc.com: “I knew Haggerty would win the fight, but I didn’t think like that. That was a nice knockout.” View this post on Instagram Getting there took work, though. Akimoto, powered by his hometown crowd, tested Haggerty with hooks in round one. A flying knee from the Brit drove him into the Circle Wall in round two, but the Japanese veteran answered with a superman punch that caught the defending champ off guard. But the momentum did not last. Akimoto charged out for round three, but “The General” met him with a right hand and then a knee that put him on the canvas. A closing burst brought the stoppage at the 42-second mark of the frame, in what may well have been Haggerty’s best night in kickboxing. Di Bella took in the whole night, and he had a clear read on what it meant. He said: “He made it look easy in Tokyo. I feel like Akimoto was at his best when he was a champ. But right now, Haggerty’s got the momentum, and as you can see, he made it look easy.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Di Bella Has A Message For Haggerty Easy is a bold word for a main event that had its scares, but Jonathan Di Bella used it twice and stood by it. The praise was only getting started. The Akimoto stoppage left the Team Di Bella Kickboxing star convinced that Haggerty – a former two-division ONE Muay Thai World Champion as well – is a more complete and more dangerous fighter in kickboxing than in the discipline that built his name. Di Bella said: “I know he likes Muay Thai, and I know Muay Thai is his first love, but I think I’ve seen him better as a kickboxer. He’s good as a kickboxer and should stay in the division. He’s very good.” View this post on Instagram Watching the Englishman’s emphatic victory has only made the ONE Strawweight Kickboxing World Champion fired up for a return to the global stage. The 30-year-old swapped the interim strap for undisputed gold last year, then defended his coveted belt against “The Fighting Rooster” Zhang Peimian at The Inner Circle 22 this past July. item.title: Alex Eala confirmed to play British player in the first round of the Tokyo Open as her draw is revealed
item.description: Alex Eala will play the penultimate tournament of her 2026 season by making her debut at the Tokyo Open. Eala has enjoyed the best season of her career so far this year, having won her first WTA title at the Washington Open , reached the fourth round of Wimbledon and broken into the top 20. Despite all of her success, Eala will not be a part of the WTA Finals this year and therefore only has two tournaments left to play in Tokyo and Hong Kong. Eala was beaten by Diana Shnaider in Ningbo , and she could face the Russian once again after the Tokyo Open draw was announced. Alex Eala could face Diana Shnaider again at the Tokyo Open The Tokyo Open is a WTA 500 tournament, and has a stacked field with the likes of Elena Rybakina , Maja Chwalinska and Naomi Osaka all featuring. Eala is the eighth seed at the Tokyo Open, and she will face British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic in the first round. Stojsavljevic is currently the world number 281, but like Eala is a former US Open junior champion. If Eala is able to overcome her British opponent, she will face either Australian Talia Gibson or a qualifier in her second round match. Eala has never faced Gibson on the WTA Tour before, but she has won both of their two previous ITF meetings. The first seeded opponent Eala could play is the aforementioned Shnaider , who beat her just this week in Ningbo. Eala has struggled against left-handed players , and this is something she will be hoping to change in Tokyo. Eala could then play Wuhan Open champion Chwalinska in the semi-finals, with world number one Rybakina potentially looming in the final. Eala has had a mixed record at WTA 500 tournaments this year, with the highlight for her coming when she won the Washington Open back in August. The Filipina will now be hoping to add to her trophy collection in Tokyo, where the main draw begins on Monday, October 26.

item.title: What Tommy Lloyd, Caleb Holt and JJ Mandaquit said after final exhibition win over Eastern Washington
item.description: Preseason play finished up for Arizona men’s basketball with a 85-54 blowout win over Eastern Washington. Caleb Holt had a very explosive 21 points performance along with four more Wildcats who scored in double figures. Here is what head coach Tommy Lloyd , Holt and JJ Mandaquit had to say following the win over Eastern Washington: Lloyd on if he got what he was looking for from the exhibitions : “I hope so. I mean, obviously, there’s a lot of good moments, and then there was a lot of teachable moments, so we got a good day off tomorrow to kind of take a breath and kind of see where we’re at, and then hopefully leading into this first game we can get a good rhythm of practice. It just felt like practice has been a little disjointed because we’ve had to stack some days off in there to make up for some extra practices we had early. So yeah, I’m excited to get back to work and keep things moving.” On Caleb Holt’s ability to forget mistakes on offense : “Caleb’s relentless, and part of the deal when you have somebody like him who’s so talented is he just gotta ride some waves. I mean, there’s gonna be some aggressive plays, and there’s gonna be some mistakes. It comes with the territory. He has five turnovers today, which is too many. We’ll take a look at where and why those are coming, and hopefully he’ll be able to learn from it. He’s been a great student so far, and a big part of the development with him is kind of teaching him what we do and why we do it. While that process is taking place, let him play with that energy and effort and those natural instincts he came here with.” On Arizona’s 20 turnovers : “I just thought it was guys being really soft and maybe a little bit selfish. We did things today that I was just like guys, I don’t know, you remember those Mad Lib books they were just kind of filling in their own words.” On Kevin Pangos joining the staff : “Kevin and I have a long history together, and it’s something he and I have been talking about for a while. I was lucky enough to recruit Kevin, and he came to Gonzaga and obviously had a great career there, and went overseas. Even had a short stint in the NBA. Just was a guy who, I don’t know, I hate the word overachieve but he got everything out of his potential he could and he’s a great student of the game and a great worker and I think he has a lot of potential as a coach so he and I have kind of been talking about this for a while and it just kind of lined up and he was ready to be done and we had an opportunity, so I’m glad we finally got it through the immigration system. It’s been a long haul, but you have to be patient with that stuff, and it’s no fault of anybody. I appreciate Rachel Blunt on our side has really did a good job helping guide me through the process and I think he’s going to be a great asset for our team over the course of this season.” On if there was any foreshadowing of Pangos having potential to become a coach : “I mean for sure. That’s an easy assumption to make

Just was a guy who, I don’t know, I hate the word overachieve but he got everything out of his potential he could and he’s a great student of the game and a great worker and I think he has a lot of potential as a coach so he and I have kind of been talking about this for a while and it just kind of lined up and he was ready to be done and we had an opportunity, so I’m glad we finally got it through the immigration system. It’s been a long haul, but you have to be patient with that stuff, and it’s no fault of anybody. I appreciate Rachel Blunt on our side has really did a good job helping guide me through the process and I think he’s going to be a great asset for our team over the course of this season.” On if there was any foreshadowing of Pangos having potential to become a coach : “I mean for sure. That’s an easy assumption to make. He grew up the son of a coach. His dad was a long time women’s university coach in Canada at York University, so he just grew up in a basketball family, and just was such a diligent worker and about all the right things that I think he’ll be a great asset.” On Arizona’s perimeter defense : “I mean, they shoot 2-14 from three. I don’t know if that’s us or them, and we got to figure it out. I think we have potential to be a good defensive team, but again I felt like we played good defense for long stretches in that game, and then we just kind of made up our own rules. With anything you do in this game, there has to be discipline. That doesn’t mean you can’t be aggressive, but you just have to temper some of this stuff with discipline and make good decisions at both ends of the floor. So we have to continue to get better at that, and that’s why seasons are long because you hope you’re not the final version of yourself in basically just outside of mid-October. So long season, and I’m looking forward to getting better.” On if he’s figured out the main rotation : “We’ll see. It depends on how practice goes next week. I mean obviously we’ve kind of been consistent thus far with who we’ve been playing and giving guys some chances. The guys that are playing right now probably are going to be the ones that are playing, unless a hail mary happens or something like that.” On the big three of Holt, Ivan Kharchenkov and Motiejus Krivas : “I’m not into big three. I’m into big big seven or eight. That’s how I always like to roll. I know who you’re talking about, they’re good players. Ivan, Caleb, and Derek today combined with 13 turnovers. That’s tough. That’s tough sledding. They’ve done a good job the first two games. So we got to figure out why, but I don’t think 13 turnovers you can just chalk up to bad luck, and so we have to look at that. That’s real stuff. For us to not score 100 points today is a little disappointing for me, but at the end of the day, exhibition, we’re learning and we got a lot of good stuff to teach.” On containing Andrew Cook : “Andrew Cook’s a hooper. He’s kind of got this crafty old man game with these step backs and these shot fake step through type things. So we just wanted to be really attentive with them, and we wanted to be physical. Obviously, he was the leading scorer two years ago, and hopefully our size and athleticism bothered him a little bit. He has the makings, looks like he’s going to be a really good player in that Big Sky conference. He’s pretty impressive.” On what he wanted out of Bryce James in the exhibitions : “Bryce has been good in practice. He got a little bit sick this week, and maybe wasn’t himself, but he didn’t start good today. I want Bryce to take advantage of this opportunity and just play with this relentless effort and energy. I think he keeps raising the standard there. I think that confidence will seep into the other parts of his game. He’s had really good stretches of practices, and so he’s right there. He’s right on the cusp of being a real player, and I’m excited to keep pushing him. He’s young, and we always knew Bryce was going to be a little bit of a late bloomer, so I’m hoping to keep pushing him and I hope he learns from today a little bit. He can’t start the game kind of the way he did today. He had a couple defensive errors. He didn’t run our first play right, and that’s stuff that he really hasn’t been doing. So hopefully, he’s just kind of a little bit of bad luck, and he’ll learn from it and be better.” On the backup centers : “That wasn’t very pretty today. I didn’t sit there and think, ‘Oh, that’s great, you know, like let’s keep building on that.’ I mean, here’s the deal: if they want to do that, they got to make it obvious for me we should do that, and the way they make that obvious for me is they go in there and kick ass. If they don’t go in there and kick ass. I try to evaluate with my eyes, not closing my eyes and dreaming. I evaluate by what I see, not what I hope I saw, and I just didn’t see it today. So those guys kind of step it up. I mean, they got to step it up. It’s time. They’re playing at Arizona. They belong here, and I expect more out of it.” On if he sees Krivas and Ugnius Jarusevicius playing at the same time : “I’m not ruling anything out. We got to be able to survive defensively if we do that. We got to be able to move the ball offensively, and today I know we didn’t do Uggi and Mo. We did Uggi and Evan, but it just felt like the ball didn’t move. The ball screens didn’t work. The guards were just doing random things, so it was hard to evaluate because I don’t know what we were doing on offense.” On JJ Mandaquit : “JJ, he was maybe one of the bright spots today. I thought he played pretty well. I thought he turned down too many shots in that second half. We had a few good possessions where the ball kind of hanged around, and maybe he found the third pass and kind of opening in the corner, and he shot faked him

item.title: Michael Owen impressed by Bayern Munich, France star Michael Olise
item.description: (Photo by Angelika Warmuth/picture alliance via Getty Images) Michael Olise has already established himself as one of the most exciting attacking players in European football, but could the Bayern Munich winger be preparing to take another major step forward with the French national team? Former England striker Michael Owen certainly believes the talent is there. Asked whether the next European Championship could be the tournament where Olise elevates his game to another level, Owen praised the Frenc hman’s outstanding season at Bayern and suggested that his performances have put him among the club’s very best pla yers. “Well, he was incredible last season, some would say Bayern Munich’s best player,” Owen told Cas ino.org . That is significant praise considering the company Olise keeps in Munich. Harry Kane has continued to produce extraordinary goalscoring numbers, while Bayern’s attack features an abundance of elite-level talent. For Olise to b e considered one of the team’s standout performers speaks volumes about the impact he has made. “Now, if you’re play ing better than Harry Kane, then you’re going some. It’s amazing to see the way he’s kicked on in his career,” Owen added. The former Ballon d’Or winner also highlighted the extraordinary depth available to France, where Olise must compete with a collection of world-class attacking players for a place in the starting lineup. “He had a great season, but the talent in the attack there, you’re leaving world-class players on the bench. It’s just incredible, that French team,” Owen said. That depth presents both a challenge and an opportunity for Oli se. Establishing himself as a regular starter for France will require him to maintain his Bayern form and deliver on the international stage, where competition for attacking positi ons is fierce. Still, Olise’s combination of creativity, dribbling, and decisive final-third contributions makes him an exciting pro spect for France’s future. If he continues to develop at Bayern Munich, the next European Championship could provide the perfect platform to demonstrate just how hig h his ceiling really is. Join the conversation! item.title: Houston Dash beat Chicago behind Leah Klenke's first goal as a pro
item.description: Leah Klenke (4) and the Dash celebrate her first goal in Friday's win over Chicago. (Daniel Bartel/NWSL via Getty Images) CHICAGO - Leah Klenke scored her first goal as a professional as the Houston Dash beat the Chicago Stars 3-1 on Friday. The Dash have earned seven points in last three road matches under interim coach Jaime Frias. Houston took a 1-0 lead in the fourth on a free kick into the box from Lisa Boattin that was stopped but Klenke got the rebound and scored. It was the fastest goal of the season for the Dash. The Dash added another goal in the 54th minute on an indirect kick from Boattin to the far post, where midfielder Maggie Graham finished with the goal. Forward Clarissa Larisey scored Houston's final goal in the 79th minute on a pass from Kiki Van Zanten. The Dash end the season at home on Nov. 1 against Portland. item.title: Aitor Mañas’s first Alavés goal denies bottom side Málaga a first win of the season
item.description: Aitor Mañas’s first Alavés goal denies bottom side Málaga a first win of the season Substitute Aitor Mañas scored his first goal for the Alavés first team in the 89th minute against Málaga at Mendizorroza. The 1-1 draw left Málaga still searching for a first win and Alavés without a victory in six matches. Málaga were a minute from victory in Vitoria on Friday night. Then an Alavés substitute intervened. The visitors went in front just before the break. Ramón Enríquez supplied the assist for Niño, who has now scored in three league matches in a row. That takes his Primera División total to four goals. Málaga coach Juanfran Funes played a single striker in Vitoria. He picked Niño because of the forward’s excellent form. Alavés dominated the ball but rarely created clear chances Alavés controlled the game with 63% possession. They also won 7 corners to Málaga’s 2. Yet clear chances were scarce. Quique Sánchez Flores sent on Toni Martínez for Mariano Díaz in the 66th minute because his side were struggling to create clear openings, according to Noticias de Álava. The decisive change came later. Mañas played 15 minutes and had 2 shots. His equaliser came when he put away a loose ball inside the area. He finished with the highest rating on the pitch, at 8.15. The point ended a run of two straight defeats for Alavés, against Atletico Madrid and Celta Vigo. Málaga stay winless in their return to the top flight The 2026-27 season is Málaga’s first in the top flight after eight years away. Funes took encouragement from the display. He described the first half as his side’s best of the season and the match as their best away performance of the campaign. He added that a first win felt close. The figures in Vitoria were more mixed. Málaga completed 385 accurate passes to Alavés’ 367, but managed only 3 shots on target. At the other end, Alfonso Herrero made 3 saves, and 6 Alavés efforts were blocked. Referee Carlos Muñiz Muñoz showed four yellow cards. Lucas Boyé and Nahuel Tenaglia were booked for Alavés. Carlos Dotor and Juan Francisco Funes Arjona were booked for Málaga. Málaga’s October fixtures also include a Copa del Rey tie against Sporting Alcázar. Their next league game is a trip to Real Betis. It is the season’s first Andalusian derby and means facing their former player Isco. Alavés head away to Barcelona in the league. Before that, they play Anaitasuna FT away in the Copa del Rey on Wednesday 28 October. The return league meeting between Málaga and Alavés is listed for Sunday 31 January 2027. item.title: Lakers outlast Clippers behind big three
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers C Walker Kessler (14) dunks the basketball during an NBA basketball game against the Los Angeles Clippers, Friday October 23, 2026 in Los Angeles, Calif. LOS ANGELES — The Lakers’ big three delivered again on Friday. This time, Austin Reaves supplied the second-half scoring burst, while Walker Kessler helped create separation with his anchoring. Reaves, Luka Dončić and Kessler combined for 73 points as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Clippers 125-117 before a sellout crowd at Crypto.com Arena, improving to 2-0. Reaves finished with 28 points and nine assists, Dončić added 23 points and Kessler contributed 22 points and six blocks. After combining for 77 points in Wednesday’s season-opening win over Golden State, the trio helped L.A. outlast the Clippers in its first crosstown matchup of the season. Rui Hachimura finished with 16 points and six rebounds in his return to L.A. He shot 5 for 14 from the field, including 3 for 6 from 3-point range, in his return. The biggest push came in the third quarter, when Reaves scored 13 points on 6-of-7 shooting and Kessler recorded two blocks. The Lakers outscored the Clippers 39-26 in the period to turn a halftime tie into a 103-90 lead. “It just felt like Walker was everywhere, in that third and really was a huge spark for us getting us a win,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Reaves had 26 points and six assists through three quarters, making nine of his first 10 shots. His efficiency helped carry the offense after Dončić opened the game shooting 2 for 10. Dončić recovered to make six of his final 11 attempts, while Reaves continued finding opportunities to score and create for teammates. The Lakers extended their advantage to 15 in the fourth quarter before the Clippers trimmed the margin. “It was a great response in the second half from everybody,” Kessler said. “But yeah, man, he’s an extremely talented player.” Getting to that point required the Lakers to slow a Clippers offense that shot 63% from the field in the first quarter. L.A. established its own presence inside early, scoring 12 of its first 16 points in the paint. But the Clippers’ shooting put the Lakers behind before their defensive activity helped change the game. Kessler accounted for three of the Lakers’ four blocks in the second quarter as they erased the deficit. By halftime, L.A. had combined for 11 steals and blocks. Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams contributed at both ends, finishing with 13 and 14 points, respectively. Redick praised their work against Darius Garland and pointed to Thybulle’s second-half 3-pointers as momentum-changing plays. The defensive effort also received an immediate contribution from Collin Sexton, who collected a steal shortly after checking in for his Lakers debut. “He gets the guys going with just his energy,” Kessler said. “That kind of stuff is contagious.” Still, the Lakers left with an issue Redick had emphasized before tipoff: taking care of the ball. The biggest push came in the third quarter, when Reaves scored 13 points on 6-of-7 shooting and Kessler recorded two blocks. The Lakers outscored the Clippers 39-26 in the period to turn a halftime tie into a 103-90 lead. “It just felt like Walker was everywhere, in that third and really was a huge spark for us getting us a win,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Reaves had 26 points and six assists through three quarters, making nine of his first 10 shots. His efficiency helped carry the offense after Dončić opened the game shooting 2 for 10. Dončić recovered to make six of his final 11 attempts, while Reaves continued finding opportunities to score and create for teammates. The Lakers extended their advantage to 15 in the fourth quarter before the Clippers trimmed the margin. “It was a great response in the second half from everybody,” Kessler said. “But yeah, man, he’s an extremely talented player.” Getting to that point required the Lakers to slow a Clippers offense that shot 63% from the field in the first quarter. L.A. established its own presence inside early, scoring 12 of its first 16 points in the paint. But the Clippers’ shooting put the Lakers behind before their defensive activity helped change the game. Kessler accounted for three of the Lakers’ four blocks in the second quarter as they erased the deficit. By halftime, L.A. had combined for 11 steals and blocks. Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams contributed at both ends, finishing with 13 and 14 points, respectively. Redick praised their work against Darius Garland and pointed to Thybulle’s second-half 3-pointers as momentum-changing plays. The defensive effort also received an immediate contribution from Collin Sexton, who collected a steal shortly after checking in for his Lakers debut. “He gets the guys going with just his energy,” Kessler said. “That kind of stuff is contagious.” Still, the Lakers left with an issue Redick had emphasized before tipoff: taking care of the ball. They committed 21 turnovers, and Redick was dissatisfied with their execution against the Clippers’ trapping defense while protecting a double-digit lead. The mistakes gave L.A. another area to address despite its productive offensive night. “We know the turnovers is a problem,” Redick said. “We’ll continue to work at it, continue to get better at it.” For a second consecutive game, however, the Lakers received enough from Dončić, Reaves and Kessler to finish with a win. Friday, their production came with a third-quarter defensive effort that gave the offense room to pull ahead.

item.title: 'Freak': Kevin Durant's instant reaction to Amen Thompson’s block vs Victor Wembanyama
item.description: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images Amen Thompson became the match-winner for the Houston Rockets against the San Antonio Spurs. The Rockets were leading the game 112-110 with just five seconds on the clock at the Moody Center, but the Spurs were on the attack. Victor Wembanyama was at the heart of it, but Thompson made an incredible block to deny the San Antonio forward, and that won the game for the Rockets. Kevin Durant reacts to ‘freak athlete’ Amen Thompson’s block vs Victor Wembanyama When Wembanyama picked up the ball, he probably thought he was going to level the score with what looked like a routine bucket for him. That game would’ve been tied at 112-112 had he scored, with less than a second left on the clock. However, Thompson pulled off the unthinkable and rose above Wembanyama to deny him. That saved the game for the Rockets. After the win, Kevin Durant, who has seen a lot of great things in his career, was asked about Thompson’s incredible block. He replied on NBA’s broadcast : “When Wemby caught the ball, I just thought he’d be a tall man and just try to rise over top. “But Twin is just a freak athlete. It’s insane how he got up so quickly to block that shot against a 7’5’’ guy being 6’7’’. What a game-saving block!” The Rockets are now 2-0 at the start of the new season, and that should give them a lot of confidence. Up next is a game against the Hawks at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
item.description: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries. The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
item.description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on Saturday It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers. Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
